intro_html: Pepper steak is the takeout order that never disappoints and never quite justifies its price. Sliced steak, green and red peppers, onion, and a glossy soy and ginger sauce over rice. Made at home it takes about half an hour once the slicing is done, and every single ingredient in it is something you can buy at a normal grocery store. Each bowl runs 577 calories and 44 grams of protein for about $4.34 a serving.
cost_closing_html: About $4.34 a bowl, which is roughly what the delivery fee alone costs on the app version. The steak is the entire expense here, so a sale on flank or sirloin swings this number more than anything else you can do.
shop_smart: Flank and sirloin are both correct here and whichever is cheaper that week is the right answer. Slice against the grain and thin, and either one comes out tender.
Bell peppers are the second biggest line. Green are cheaper than red almost every week, so if the budget is tight, run all green and the dish loses nothing but a little color.

Cornstarch is the cheapest ingredient in the recipe and the most important one. It thickens the sauce into that glossy coat and it also velvets the beef if you toss the slices in a little before searing.
Soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and honey are all pantry bottles that last through many batches. Once they are on the shelf, the per-bowl cost of this sauce is close to zero.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Freeze the steak for about 30 minutes so it firms up, then slice it thin against the grain. Toss the slices with a spoonful of the cornstarch and a splash of the soy sauce and let them sit while you prep everything else.

Whisk the rest of the soy sauce, rice vinegar, honey, sesame oil, and remaining cornstarch together with a little water. Having the sauce ready in a cup before you start is the whole secret to stir frying, because once the pan is hot there is no time to measure anything.
Get a large skillet very hot with the vegetable oil and sear the beef in batches, about 90 seconds a side. Pull it out while it is still slightly underdone. It will finish in the sauce.
Add the sliced peppers, onion, and jalapeno to the same pan and cook hard for 3 to 4 minutes. You want them blistered at the edges and still crisp in the middle, not soft.
Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then pour in the sauce and let it bubble and thicken.
Return the beef and any juices, toss everything together for a minute, and season with paprika, salt, and plenty of black pepper.
portion_html: Weigh the rice into the containers first, then set the skillet on the scale, subtract the empty weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. That gets an even share of steak into every bowl, which matters more here than in almost any other recipe because the peppers are easy to over-scoop. Each portion lands at 577 calories.

head.description: Pepper steak with rice, sliced beef and bell peppers in a glossy soy ginger sauce, rebuilt for 14 meal prep servings at about $4.34 a bowl.
head.keywords: pepper steak, beef and pepper stir fry, chinese takeout at home, steak rice bowl, budget meal prep, high protein meal prep
recipeIngredient: 5.25 lb beef flank or sirloin steak
steps: Firm the steak in the freezer, slice thin against the grain, and toss with cornstarch and soy sauce.
Cook the rice and whisk the sauce ingredients together before you heat the pan.
Sear the beef in batches in a very hot skillet and set aside slightly underdone.
Stir fry the peppers, onion, and jalapeno hard, then add garlic and ginger.
Pour in the sauce, thicken, return the beef, and toss.
Weigh rice and stir fry into 14 containers.
